subject: History
description: Imperial Cholas, Rajaraja I, Rajendra I, naval power, Brihadeeswara temple

questions.stem: The greatest Chola emperor who built the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur was:

options.option_text: Rajendra Chola I, the naval emperor
Kulottunga Chola I, of later phase

questions.explanation: RAJARAJA CHOLA I (r. 985-1014 CE) — built the magnificent BRIHADEESWARA TEMPLE / Rajarajeshwaram (1010 CE) at Thanjavur (UNESCO World Heritage; 'Great Living Chola Temples'). Granite shikhara ~66 m, single capstone weighs ~80 tonnes. Conquered: Kerala, Sri Lanka (north), Maldives. Standardised Chola revenue + administration. Distractor 1: Aditya Chola I (c. 871-907) was the founder of imperial line. Distractor 3: Rajendra (his son) built temple at Gangaikondacholapuram. Distractor 4: Kulottunga (1070-1120) was later.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Rajendra Chola I, son of Rajaraja, took which title after his triumphant Ganga expedition?

options.option_text: Gangaikonda Chola, conqueror of the Ganges
Vikrama Chola, the brave conqueror title

questions.explanation: RAJENDRA CHOLA I (r. 1014-1044 CE) — most famous Chola. ~1019-22 CE marched north, defeated Pala king Mahipala (Bengal), brought Ganga water back to his capital. Took title GANGAIKONDA CHOLA (= 'Chola who conquered the Ganges'). Built new capital GANGAIKONDA CHOLAPURAM with a great Shiva temple + a giant tank ('Cholaganga'). Also led NAVAL EXPEDITIONS to Srivijaya (Sumatra, Malaya) ~1025 CE — first Indian to project sea power that far. Distractor 1 is Aditya II Karikala's title.

questions.stem: Chola local self-government was famously developed at the village level via:
questions.explanation: Chola village government — 3 tiers: UR (general village assembly of all classes); SABHA (or Mahasabha) — assembly of brahmin agraharas (brahmin-only Brahmadeya villages); NAGARAM — assembly of merchants/traders. UTTIRAMERUR INSCRIPTIONS (Parantaka I, 919 + 921 CE) — fascinating record of how Sabhas were elected: kuda-olai (pot-ticket) lottery from qualified candidates' names written on palm leaves. Variyams (committees) for irrigation, gardens, justice, treasury. Local self-government ahead of its time. Distractor 1 is Vedic-age. Distractor 3 is central, not village.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Cholas were the most powerful naval force in their day. Rajendra Chola's naval expedition reached:
questions.explanation: Rajendra I led naval expedition (~1025 CE) against SRIVIJAYA empire (Sumatra-Malaya-Java; Buddhist thalassocracy controlling Strait of Malacca). Defeated king Sangrama Vijayottunga Varman, captured Kadaram (Kedah), wealth + ports. Aim: secure trade routes to China. The Cholas dominated Indian Ocean trade for ~200 years. Also expanded to Sri Lanka. Distractor 1: Cholas didn't go to Persia. Distractor 4: Indian-East Africa trade existed but was Arab-mediated, not Chola-led.

questions.stem: The famous CHOLA BRONZES (Nataraja, etc.) were cast using which technique?
questions.explanation: LOST-WAX (cire perdue) method — wax sculpture made first → coated with clay → fired (wax melts out, leaving cavity) → molten bronze poured in → clay broken to reveal final bronze. Allows fine detail. CHOLA BRONZES — pinnacle of Indian sculpture. Most famous: NATARAJA (Shiva as Lord of Dance) — multi-armed, leg raised in dance pose, fire halo, Apasmara (demon of ignorance) trampled. Also Parvati, Vishnu, saints (Bhakti period — Alvars + Nayanars). Adopted from earlier Pallava + Ganga work but perfected by Cholas.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Chola kingdom's CAPITAL CITY founded by Rajendra I was:
questions.explanation: Original Chola capital — THANJAVUR (under Rajaraja). Rajendra I shifted to GANGAIKONDA CHOLAPURAM after his Ganga expedition (~1025 CE). Built a great Shiva temple there (Brihadeeswara II). Also built a vast tank — Cholaganga — by carrying water from the Ganga (symbolic). Capital remained until late Chola period. Now in Ariyalur district, Tamil Nadu (UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples, 2004). Distractor 1: Madurai = Pandyan capital. Distractor 3: Kanchipuram = Pallava capital.

questions.stem: The Chola dynasty's eventual DECLINE in 13th century was mainly due to:

options.option_text: Defeat by the rising Mughal empire
Rise of Pandyas and Hoysalas in south
Black plague pandemic spread of era

questions.explanation: Cholas declined ~late 12th-early 13th c. CE under combined pressure from rising PANDYAS (Madurai, especially Maravarman Sundara Pandya, Jatavarman Sundara Pandya) and HOYSALAS (Karnataka, esp. Vira Ballala II). Rajadhiraja Chola III defeated by Pandyas ~1279 CE — last Chola king. Distractor 1 — Mughals came centuries later (16th c.). Distractor 3 — Black Death was 14th c., Eurasia-wide, not Chola-centric. Distractor 4 — Cholas were Shaivites; Buddhism had declined long before.
